questions.prompt_markup: Why does the graph of y = log(x² - 1) have two separate branches?

choices.text: Every logarithm graph has two branches, one on each side of its asymptote.
Its domain is x < -1 or x > 1: x² - 1 > 0 on two separate intervals.
log(x² - 1) is undefined at x = 0 only, which splits the graph in two.
Its domain is -1 < x < 1, an interval split in two at x = 0.

questions.correct_answer: Its domain is x < -1 or x > 1: x² - 1 > 0 on two separate intervals.
questions.grading_note: A logarithm needs a positive input. The others reverse the domain or overgeneralize (y = log x has one branch).
